# Fitness App Onboarding Flow Design Documentation

## Introduction
This document outlines the complete onboarding flow for our new fitness app designed to motivate users and get them started with their health goals through personalized workout plans, diet suggestions, progress tracking, and a supportive community. The goal of this design is to create an inviting experience that guides first-time signups seamlessly into the heart of our application where they can begin making positive changes in their lives.

## Onboarding Flow Overview
The onboarding flow starts with users opening the app and ends when a user completes signing up or deciding to navigate away from the screen without creating an account. The process consists of five screens: Welcome Screen, Introduction Video (optional), Fitness Goals Setup, Diet & Nutrition Overview, and Sign-Up Confirmation with Continue Flow Options.

### 1. **Welcome Screen**
The first screen the user sees when opening our app is a visually appealing welcome message that introduces them to what our fitness journey will look like within these walls of technology:
> "Embrace your inner strength and embark on an exciting, fun-filled path towards better health with [App Name] - Your personalized companion in achieving wellbeing goals!" 

The screen is designed using a vibrant color palette that promotes positivity. It also features our app logo at the top right corner and provides three options: "Start My Fitness Journey" (continue to Introduction Video), "Learn More About Us," or exit without signing up.

### 2. **Introduction Video**
If a user chooses to watch an introduction video, they're presented with this short animation that showcases the app in action and highlights key features:
> The screen displays our animated introductory storyline featuring diverse users of different ages engaging in various activities within our community while achieving their fitness goals. We also see a brief overview of how to navigate through the application, including setting up personalized workout plans or tracking progress on existing ones. This video ends with an invitation for them to create their account and begin using [App Name].

### 3. **Fitness Goals Setup**
After watching our introduction video (or skipping it), the next screen prompts users to set up personalized fitness goals:
> The user is asked what they want to achieve with this app, such as weight loss or muscle gain, and encouraged to provide details like their age, gender, height, desired outcome time frame, preferred workout times, etc. They can also select the type of exercises (cardio/strength training) that best suits them based on our recommendations. After this information is gathered from users' responses, we generate a personalized plan with suggested activities and show it to them for their approval or further customization if needed.

### 4. **Diet & Nutrition Overview**
If the user opts not to set up fitness goals on this screen but wishes to learn more about dietary needs, they are presented with a brief overview of our nutrition guidance system:
> The UI shows an infographic-style presentation that explains how different food groups contribute towards meeting their health and wellness objectives. They can also see recommendations for meal plans based on the user's fitness goals (if provided) or general advice to maintain a balanced diet while working out regularly using our app’s features like tracking calorie intake, suggesting recipes with ingredients they have at home in their pantry.

### 5. **Sign-Up Confirmation and Continue Flow Options**
After the user has completed all necessary information (fitness goals or dietary preferences), we invite them to create an account:
> The screen displays a friendly welcome message, followed by our signup form that collects essential details such as full name, email address, password confirmation, and age. A checkbox is included for users who agree with the app's terms of service (ToS) before submitting their information via an easy-to-use input field or voice command option if supported by device capabilities:

# Go-to-Market Plan for Productivity SaaS Tool for Freelancers

## Executive Summary
This document outlines our go-to-market plan (GTM) to launch a new productivity Software as a Service (SaaS) tool designed specifically for freelancers. Our target audience consists of independent professionals who seek efficiency and organization in their work processes without the overhead costs associated with traditional business solutions. This SaaS platform will provide an all-inclusive, user-friendly interface that streamlines project management, time tracking, client communication, and financial planning tailored to freelancer needs.

## Target Audience 
Our primary target audience includes:
* Freelancers across various fields such as writing, designing, consulting, programming etc. who seek an all-inclusive platform that enhances their productivity while reducing the overhead costs associated with traditional business solutions.
* Small Business Owners (SBOs) and Entrepreneurs: SBOs often operate on a freelance basis due to limited resources or as part of agile work culture within startups, thus requiring similar tools for efficiency. 
* Students who wish to supplement their income through freelancing while keeping track of deadlines across multiple projects and clients.   

## Market Analysis & Competition  
The productivity SaaS market is highly competitive with several established players offering comprehensive solutions, such as Togit, Upwork's platform for SME owners or Fiverr which offers a freelancing community among other services. Our differentiator will be the focus on simplicity and affordability while maintaining robust features necessary to manage projects effectively across various fields of work.

## Pricing Structure  
Our SaaS productivity tool for Freelancers, 'Freely', offers three pricing tiers that cater to varying needs: 
* **Basic Tier ($8/month)** - This package includes a project management dashboard with task and calendar features. It also provides essential time-tracking functionalities which freelancers can use for personal finance tracking purposes, such as invoicing clients or keeping track of hours spent on each client's workload.
* **Pro Tier ($20/month)** - This package includes all the Basic tier features and adds premium project management capabilities with advanced collaboration tools that allow freelancers to collaborate effectively within a team, share files securely in real-typed, or asynchronously communicate through integrated messaging system. It also provides access to customizable templates for client proposals, contracts, quotes etc., and integrates seamlessly with popular accounting software like QuickBooks Pro/Advanced Accounts (which freelancers can use at a discounted rate).
* **Premium Tier ($30/month)** - This package includes all the features of both Basic and Pro tiers, adds an AI-powered work assistant that helps in prioritizing tasks based on deadlines or difficulty level. It also provides access to exclusive webinars with productivity experts for freelancers who seek additional guidance beyond our platform's core offerings.

## Launch Timeline & Marketing Plan (90-Day Launch)  
* **Month 1**: Finalize the MVP based on user feedback and beta testing results, develop marketing campaign materials such as website banners/sliders, landing pages for social media ads. Start pre-launch activities like creating a mailing list of interested freelancers through our platform's signup form or reaching out to industry bloggers in different fields for guest posting on their websites and sharing the link back to 'Freely'.
* **Month 05**: Official launch with initial offerings based on feedback from beta testing users. Start social media ad campaign targeting freelancers via LinkedIn, Facebook Groups & Reddit communities that are relevant in various fields of work where our tool is applicable and create an email marketing plan to nurture leads generated through the website banners/sliders shared on different platforms like Instagram or Twitter.
* **Month 06**: Start a referral program for freelancers who invite friends, colleagues or family members with similar needs into using our platform in exchange of discounts and free credits to the Pro & Premium tiers upon their first month's subscription renewal after joining.
* **Month 07**: Host a webinar series featuring productivity experts who will share tips, tricks on how freelancers can manage projects effectively with our platform as well as best practices in time management and client communication skills that complement the use of 'Freely'. This is also an opportunity to gather feedback for further enhancement.
* **Month 08**: Begin a customer success program where we provide personalized consultation sessions between freelancers who have joined our platform, experienced challenges in project management or financial planning and are considering switching from competitors' platforms that don’t cater to their needs as best-in-class SaaS productivity tool.
* **Month 09**: Conduct a comprehensive review of user feedback received during the first three months, identify areas for improvement in UI/UX design and fix bugs reported by users if any; launch new features or enhancements based on customer's suggestions as well to maintain our relevance amidst competitors.
* **Month 12**: Evaluate overall performance metrics such as growth of active user base, monthly recurring revenue (MRR), and lifetime value (LTV) against target numbers set at the beginning of this plan; optimize marketing strategies accordingly for sustained success beyond our first year in operation.

## Partnerships & Collaborations  
Our SaaS productivity tool will actively seek partnerships with other businesses relevant to freelancers, such as co-working spaces or professional networking events that cater specifically towards the independent workforce like Freelancer's Marketplace. We would also consider collaborating with universities on student projects where students can get real world experience working alongside experienced professionals while still being in a learning environment for entrepreneurship and business skills development, thereby creating an opportunity to promote 'Freely' as the go-to SaaS productivity tool amongst upcoming talent. 

## Conclusion  
This comprehensive GTM plan sets out our strategy towards launching Freely - aimed at providing freelancers with a simple yet powerful and affordable solution for managing their projects, time tracking, client communication & financial planning needs effectively while competing against established players in the market. By focusing on simplicity, personalization through customer success program as well as strategic partnerships we hope to capture significant share of freelancers across various fields who seek a comprehensive all-inclusive solution for their productivity management needs without compromising affordability or efficiency while growing our user base and revenue in the process.

# Blog REST API Design for SimpleBlogs Platform

## Introduction
This document outlines our design for a simple blog platform using Representational State Transfer (REST) principles and Flask as the server-side framework in Python, with JWT (JSON Web Tokens) based authentication. The data models will be designed to facilitate CRUD operations on posts and comments easily. This API is aimed at providing full endpoints for creating new blogs, adding content within a post or comment, reading existing information, updating it as needed, and deleting entries when appropriate.

## Data Models (Models)
To represent the data related to our simpleblog platform effectively, we will define two primary models: `Post` and `Comment`. Both are inherently linked through foreign keys in a relational database such as PostgreSQL or MySQL since they share an author-toindependent association. For simplicity's sake, this design assumes that each comment can be associated with only one post but not vice versa (i.e., many comments per post).

### 1. `Post` Model
```python
class Post(db.Model):
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(256), nullable=False)
    content = db.Column(db.Text(), nullable=False)
    author_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('user.id'))  # Associated with a user account (Authenticated User).
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, server_default=db.func.now())
    
    def __init__(self, title, content, author_id):
        self.title = title
        self.content = content
        self.author_id = author_id
        
```
### 2. `Comment` Model

# Small E-commerce Website Security Review Checklist

## Introduction
This checklist serves to guide security professionals and website administrators in conducting thorough security reviews for small e-commerce websites. It covers critical areas such as payment handling, user data protection, and common vulnerabilities that need regular assessment. By following this comprehensive review process, you can significantly mitigate risks associated with online transactions and safeguard your business against potential cyber threats.

## Payment Handling Security Checklist 
Ensure the integrity of payment systems by examining these aspects:
- **Payment Gateway Integration**: Verify that secure, reliable third-party gateways are used for processing payments. Ensure they comply with industry standards such as PCI DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard). 
- **Encryption and Tokenization**: Confirm the implementation of SSL/TLS encryption to protect sensitive data during transmission between clients, servers, payment gateways, etc. Check for tokenized or dummy credit card numbers in test environments to prevent misuse if credentials are compromised.
- **Multi-factor Authentication (MFA)**: Make sure that MFA is enabled and enforced on all administrative accounts related to the e-commerce platform'infrastructure such as database access, server management interfaces etc., for an added layer of security against unauthorized access attempts. 
- **Payment Logging & Monitoring**: Establish comprehensive logging mechanisms that capture every transaction attempt and review logs regularly to identify potential fraudulent activities or anomalies in payment processing patterns (e.g., unusually high transactions from a specific IP address). Consider employing automated tools for continuous monitoring of real-time threats if resources allow it.
- **PCI Compliance Audit**: Carry out regular internal and external PCI compliance audits to ensure continued adherence with the necessary security measures against unauthorized access, data breaches or misuse involving credit card information processing within your website infrastructure. Refer to resources such as "What is a PA-DSS Compliant Payment Application?" by Visa for guidance on compliance best practices and documentation requirements (https://www.visa.com/resources/for_businesses/whatispadescompliancethroughputguidebook).

## User Data Security Checklist 
Protect user data effectively with these measures:
- **Data Collection**: Ensure that the website collects only essential personal information from users, such as names and email addresses. Avoid requesting unnecessary details like financial statements or social security numbers (SSNs). In case of required sensitive info collection, provide clear disclosures about data usage policies to gain user consent before proceeding with their submissions on your site.
- **Encryption & Tokenization**: Implement SSL/TLS encryption for all personal information collected and stored within the website's infrastructure as well during transit between clients (browsers) and servers via HTTPS protocol, using strong ciphers like AES256 or ChaCha20. Employ tokenized representations of personally identifiable user data to further minimize exposure risks in case your systems get compromised by malicious actors who may gain access to database backups etc.
- **Data Retention Policy**: Establish a clear and compliant policy regarding the duration for which personal information will be retained once users have ceased using or interacting with your e-commerce platform (e.g., 90 days). Ensure that this data is securely deleted from all storage mediums, including backups after its retention period has lapsed to avoid potential misuse by unauthorized parties in the future should they obtain access through breaches or other means of compromise within your network infrastructure.
- **Regular Access Reviews**: Periodically review user account permissions and roles with respect to data stored under their names/IDs on a regular basis (e.g., monthly). Remove unused accounts, update permission levels as needed based upon current activity or changes in business requirements while ensuring that essential access remains available for authorized personnel such as administrators who need it occasionally but not constantly due to changing job responsibilities etc..
- **Data Sharing & Transfer**: If you plan on sharing user data with third parties (e.g., analytics providers), ensure they comply with relevant privacy regulations like GDPR or CCPA prioritizing users' rights over their personal information protection at all times when doing so externally through API integrations etc.. Always obtain explicit consent from the end-users before proceeding to share any sensitive data outside your own infrastructure.

## Common Vulnerability Checklist 
Assess common vulnerabilities and implement proactive measures against them:
1. **SQL Injection**: Scan for possible SQL injection points within application code where user inputs are used directly in query statements without proper sanitization or parameterized queries (prepared statements). Test these areas by inputting malicious payloads to uncover potential exploits that can lead unauthorized access, data tampering etc..
2. **Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)**: Inspect all user-generated content displayed on your website pages for vulnerabilities where attackers may inject harmful scripts into these inputs with malicious intentions like session hijackings or phishing scams targeted towards users directly via their browsers etc..
3. **Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)**: Identify any form submissions made by your website visitors that might be prone to CSRF attacks where attackers impersonate legitimate requests from authenticated users within trusted domains and trick them into performing unintended actions on behalf of the real user without their knowledge or consent.
4. **Broken Authentication/Session Management**: Verify proper implementation of session management mechanisms including secure cookie attributes (e.g., HttpOnly, Secure flags) along with appropriate server-side validation routines for authentication tokens ensuring that sessions cannot be stolen easily via cross-site request forgery or other similar attacks etc..

# Mobile Application Development Recommendation for Startup: React Native vs Flutter

## Introduction
A startup with two founders intending to develop their first mobile application must carefully select the most appropriate framework that aligns well with their project's specific needs, timeline, and skill set. This research summary compares *React Native* by Facebook and Meta (formerly known as Instagram) against Google’ extraneous subsidiary platform, Flutter. Both frameworks offer unique advantages for mobile application development but excel in different aspects that can significantly influence a startup's success trajectory.

## Project Requirements Analysis 
Before delving into the comparison of React Native and Flutter, it is essential to outline our hypothetical project requirements:
- The app should be visually appealing with smooth animations for user engagement.
- It needs a simple authentication system that ensures secure access control across multiple platforms (iOS & Android).
- A basic yet flexible architecture allowing future expansion without significant rewrites would benefit the startup's long-term plans.

## React Native: Pros and Cons 
React Native, developed by Facebook in collaboration with Microsoft, is an established framework that allows developers to build mobile apps using JavaScript and React for both iOS and Android platforms from a single codebase. Here are its pros and cons concerning our project's requirements:

### Advantages of Using React Native: 
- **Cross-platform compatibility** - One significant benefit is the ability to write once, deploy on multiple platforms simultaneously without needing separate development efforts for each platform. This can significantly reduce timeframes when developing a mobile application and allows developers with JavaScript knowledge (which are abundant) to leverage their skills effectively in React Native environment.
- **Strong community support** - The framework has an extensive open-source ecosystem, providing access to pre-built components for various functionalities like navigation, which can speed up development time significantly and ensure consistency across platforms with respect to design elements such as buttons or icons. This robust library of third-party tools enhances the app's aesthetics without much extra coding effort from developers themselves.
- **Performance** - React Native apps have decent performance, especially for simple applications that don’t require heavy computations on each frame update. The framework uses native components where possible and JavaScript ones when necessary to maintain smooth animations which align with our project's visual appeal requirements in the app design. 

### Disadvantages of Using React Native:  
- **Performance bottlenecks** - For more complex applications requiring heavy computations or high frame rates for every animation, such as a game application that demands real-time physics calculations and smooth graphics rendering to maintain user engagement levels. In this case, the performance might suffer when using React Native because of its JavaScript engine's limitations compared with native code execution speed on each device platform.
- **Limited access** - The framework does not provide direct control over some lower level aspects such as accessing or modifying system resources directly like audio and video playback controls which may be essential for the startup’s project needs, thus requiring additional libraries that could increase complexity in development efforts while maintaining consistency across platforms. 
- **Learning Curve** - Although React Native has a relatively friendly learning curve due to its JavaScript base, it still requires developers with some experience or knowledge of Javascript and modern web technologies such as ES6+ syntax standards for effective utilization within the framework without any major issues in implementation complexity while maintaining code quality. 
- **Limited platform customisation** - React Native does not offer extensive options to modify native components directly, which may limit our ability to tailor UI elements specific to each Android or iOS version if necessary beyond a basic level of modification via the framework's built-in styling capabilities and third-party libraries.

## Flutter: Pros and Cons 
Google’s open-source mobile application development platform, also known as Dart with an emphasis on UI (User Interface), was designed to offer developers a more native experience across iOS, Android, macOS desktop, web browser, and standalone Linux app. Here are its pros and cons concerning our project's requirements:

### Advantages of Using Flutter: 
- **Highly performant** - With the ability to compile Dart code into highly optimized native components for each platform individually using a single source codebase in which developers can directly control all aspects at runtime. This ensures smooth animations and real-time physics calculations required by our project without any compromise on performance, even with heavy computations or complex app logic that demands high frame rates to maintain user engagement levels throughout the application's lifetime.
- **Customizable UI** - Flutter provides more options for customization of native components directly through Dart code allowing developers greater control over UX design elements while ensuring consistent look and feel across platforms, which align well with our project requirements in terms of visual appeal without compromising on aesthetics or user experience. 
- **Learning Curve** - Flutter may have higher learning curve compared to React Native due to the requirement for Dart language proficiency; however, considering that both founders are developers and with proper training resources available online (e.g., Udemy courses), this challenge can be overcome without much difficulty in a short span of time while maintaining code quality throughout development efforts within reasonable complexity levels as required by our project needs.
- **Better platform customization** - Flutter allows for more extensive control over native components directly through Dart language syntax, which provides greater flexibility when tailoring UX design elements specific to each Android or iOS version beyond a basic level of modification provided in React Native framework with its built-in styling capabilities and third-party libraries. This aligns well with our project requirements for customization if necessary while maintaining code quality throughout development efforts within reasonable complexity levels as required by the startup's needs without compromising on any aspect such as security or access to system resources like audio/video playback controls which Flutter provides direct control over via platform channels.

## Introduction
This comprehensive plan outlines how to launch an effective paid ad campaign on Instagram using data-driven audience targeting, strategic budget allocation, engaging ad copy, and measurable success metrics. The goal of this first campaign is not only to attract new customers but also to drive website traffic for a boutique clothing retailer specializing in eco-friendly fashion accessories called "Green Threads."

To create an ad that resonates with our ideal customer, we need to understand who they are and where they spend their time online. # CSV to JSON Converter CLI Tool - README and Setup Guide
---

## Introduction
This document serves as the definitive guide for setting up and using our open-source Python command-line interface (CLI) tool, `csvjson`, which converts comma-separated values (CSV) files into their equivalent JSON format. The utility is designed to be simple yet robust, ensuring compatibility with a wide array of CSV structures while offering customization options for those requiring more control over the conversion process.

## Installation and Setup
Before diving right into using `csvjson`, you must install it in your Python environment:
```bash
pip install csvjson
```
If this tool is not already installed, run the above command to fetch it from PyPI (Python Package Index). Once installation completes successfully, we are ready to proceed.

## Usage and Options
`csvjson` provides a straightforward syntax for converting CSV files into JSON format directly within your terminal or console window:
```bash
csvjson [options] <input_file> > output_file.json
```
Here's what each part of the command means, with further details provided below in this section and Subsections 2-5 as they unfold through usage examples and explanations for more advanced options available within `csvjson`. Please refer to Section 6 on troubleshooting common issues encountered during conversion. Finally, we conclude our guide by detailing how contributors can engage with the project via Code of Conduct in Subsection 7.

### Basic Usage Example: Convert CSV without Options
To convert a simple CSV file named `sample_data.csv` into JSON format and save it as `output.json`, execute the following command:
```bash hallmark bash
csvjson sample_data.csv > output.json
```
The above example assumes that your input CSV is located in the same directory from which you run this conversion tool, or alternatively, provide an absolute path to locate it correctly within different directories. The resulting JSON file will have indented structure for better readability and maintain a consistent format across all `csvjson` executions on identical data sets unless otherwise specified through options discussed further below in Subsections 3-5.

### Customizing Output with Options (Subsection Details Included)
#### `--no-indent`: Suppresses Indentation for Minimalistic JSON Format
When you prefer a minimal, non-indented format of the resulting JSON output that mimics its structure as it would appear in an array without unnecessary whitespace or indentation delimiters:
```bash
csvjson --no-indent sample_data.csv > output.json
```
#### `--fields` / `-f`: Specify Fields to Include/Exclude from Conversion (Subsection Details Included)
To include specific fields in the JSON representation of your CSV data, use this option:
```bash
csvjson --fields field1,field2 sample_data.csv > output.json
```
For excluding certain columns during conversion to streamline processed information for those requiring a more concise dataset format (Subsection Details Included):
```bash
csvjson -e columnX,columnY sample_data.csv > cleaned_output.json
```
#### `--array`: Convert CSV Rows into Array Format Instead of Objects 
When you need to represent your converted data as arrays instead of objects:
```bash
csvjson --array sample_data.csv > array_output.json
```
Note that this option may affect the compatibility with downstream tools expecting object-based JSON structures (Subsection Details Included). Make sure to consider how subsequent processing steps will handle your data before opting for arrays over objects in `csvjson` outputs when using `--array`.

#### `--date`: Standardize Date Formats within Conversion Outputs 
To ensure consistency across the dates present throughout CSV records, and prevent potential parsing issues during JSON conversion due to varying date formats:
```bash
csvjson --date 'YYYY-MM-DD' sample_data.csv > standardized_output.json
```
Note that this option is particularly useful when dealing with datasets featuring mixed or ambiguous dates within their records (Subsection Details Included). For further details on handling date parsing and formatting, refer to Section 6: Troubleshooting Common Issues below where we cover potential errors associated with time-related data.

### Advanced Options for Customizing Outputs Further & Handling Complex CSV Structures (Subsections Detailed)
#### `--quote`: Handle Special Characters in Field Values by Surrounding Them With Quotes 
To prevent issues stemming from special characters within your field values that may otherwise be misinterpreted during JSON conversion, enclose these fields with quotes using the following command:
```bash
csvjson --quote sample_data.csv > quoted_output.json
```
#### `--escape`: Escape Characters Within Field Values (Subsection Details Included)
To escape characters within field values that may potentially cause parsing issues or misinterpretations during conversion, enable this option by executing:
```bash0 bash
csvjson --escape sample_data.csv > escaped_output.json
```
#### `--header`: Retain Original CSV Headers as JSON Field Names (Subsection Details Included)
To maintain the original headers from your input CSV file within their respective field names in resulting JSON output, use this option:
```bash0 bash
csvjson --header sample_data.csv > header-preserved_output.json
```
#### `--recursive`: Enable Recursive Conversion of Nested CSV Files into Deeply Nested JSON Structures 
When working with nested or hierarchical data structures within your input CSV files, enable the recursive conversion process by using:
```bash0 bash
csvjson --recursive sample_data.csv > recursive-output.json
```
Note that this option is best suited for datasets featuring interrelated records across multiple levels of hierarchy (Subsection Details Included). For more information on working with nested CSV data and understanding the resulting JSON output, refer to Section 5: Advanced Options Detailed Explanation below where we delve deeper into these features.

## Troubleshooting Common Issues Encountered During Conversion Processes (Subsection Details Included)
When issues arise during conversion or usage of `csvjson`, here are some common problems and their respective solutions to help you maintain a smooth workflow:
#### Error Handling When Input CSV Files Contain Mixed Date Formats 
In scenarios where your input data contains mixed date formats, the `--date` option may not be able to standardize all instances. In such cases, consider pre-processing or post-conversion steps for normalizing dates before using `csvjson`. Alternatively, explore options like [Pandas](https://pandas.pydata.org/) which offer more sophisticated date parsing capabilities (Subsection Details Provided).
#### Handling Special Characters Within CSV Field Values 
If special characters within your field values are causing issues during the conversion process despite using `--quote` or `--escape`, consider cleaning these fields manually prior to running `csvjson`. Additionally, review and adjust settings related to quoting delimiters (`--quotes`) if applicable. For further guidance on handling such scenarios effectively while preserving data integrity (Subsection Details Provided), refer back to Section 3: Customizing Output with Options Detailed Explanation where we discuss these options in more depth.
